sense: someone of the same age or standing

terms.gloss: someone of the same age; a contemporary
terms.grammar: noun (an adjective used as one), third declension; with a genitive or a possessive
evidence: Cic. Sen. 10: adulēscēns ita dīlēxī senem ut aequālem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Peers by age: aequālis meus, someone my age; aequālēs, children of one’s own age. As an adjective it means equal (see equal).

terms.gloss: an equal, a match; one of the same rank
evidence: Cic. Sen. 7: parēs … cum paribus facillimē congregantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Peers by standing rather than age. Lewis & Short gives it, with aequālis as a synonym, for “equal in station or age”.

phrases.latin: deinde aequālibus dēlectantur libenterque sē cum iīs congregant dantque sē ad lūdendum fābellārumque audītiōne dūcuntur
phrases.english: then they enjoy children their own age, gladly join them, give themselves up to play, and are drawn by hearing stories

phrases.latin: parēs vetere prōverbiō cum paribus facillimē congregantur
phrases.english: equals, as the old proverb says, flock together most easily
